clue.text: It gets one down to get out of the habit!

definitions.text: It gets one down to get out of the habit!

parts.words: It gets one down to get out of the habit!
parts.note: reads like a cure for an addiction, but 'habit' is clothing and 'one down' points at the neighbouring light, a person who wears nothing

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person kick a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like an addiction; here it means clothes. 'One down' is the solution at 1 Down, a person wearing nothing, which is what this person becomes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist strips off all clothing, the 'habit' of dress, as a matter of principle.

parts.note: could describe a person with an empty diary, but literally means someone wearing no clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing on' suggests a free evening; read literally it means wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, so has no garments on at all.

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of the preceding words into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm has torn up an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a touring band of performers, a theatrical company.

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters of sceptres are taken in another order

explanation.surface: Someone admires what different royal sceptres are worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard, to look up to them.

clue.text: One who sees the future of episcopal seat's first rectory

parts.note: a bishop's seat, the area of their authority, is a see

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of rectory

explanation.surface: A prophet's prediction for the cathedral and its leading parsonage.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEE is a bishop's diocese or seat; 'first' takes R from 'rectory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is said to foresee what is coming.

indicators.note: backing a horse suggests a bet, but here it means the word murder is read from its end

explanation.surface: Betting on a Grand National winner is a killing idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum won the Grand National, the famous steeplechase run at Aintree near Liverpool, three times; its name is MURDER spelt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum was a racehorse that won the Grand National at Aintree in 1973, 1974 and 1977.

clue.text: The Spanish are not odd going one after another

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
a number that is not odd is even

explanation.surface: Spanish people are perfectly normal when queuing in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is visual: the number 11 is written as one digit 1 after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure 11 is two ones written side by side, a numeral following its twin.

clue.text: Wheel of fortune allowed to get in the way

indicators.note: get in means one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a route is the way you travel
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Fate is permitted to block someone's path.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game in which a ball settles on a spinning numbered wheel, deciding fortunes.

parts.note: sounds like tidy hidden assassins, but 'neat' is the old word for cattle and the cloak is the bullfighter's cape

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so 'neat killers' are slayers of bulls, who carry a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighters who make the kill in the ring, working with a red cape.

clue.text: Way in pets flick up thick slice of bread

parts.note: a door is a way into a building

indicators.note: flick up means the word pets is turned over and read backwards

explanation.surface: Animals at the entrance send a crust flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is British slang for a very thickly cut piece from a loaf.

indicators.note: violence done to the word Ulster breaks its letters up and rearranges them

explanation.surface: A response to unrest in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is a name for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or consequence that follows from some cause.

explanation.surface: Someone vouching for a travel pass.
explanation.definitionFit: One who vouches is a person giving assurance; a coupon exchangeable for goods is the other sense.

clue.text: Great to have last scrap at meal time

indicators.note: one word holding another, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: super means great

indicators.note: last takes only the final letter of scrap

explanation.surface: It is great to get the final morsel at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening meal, eaten late in the day.

clue.text: A warning on top of the brow

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of an incoming ball
the head is the top of something

explanation.surface: A caution placed on the top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brow' could be a hilltop, fitting the surface; here it is the part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow is the part of the face above the eyes.

clue.text: Try understanding and listen to the old

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is tries it
ken means knowledge or understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt comprehension by paying attention to elders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen to the old' means 'listen' in an old-fashioned word, not paying heed to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to pay attention or heed.

explanation.surface: Tension as described by a sentence's grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stretch' is slang for a prison term, the 'sentence' meant here.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull taut or overextend; a spell in prison is the slang second sense.

explanation.surface: A question of whether an object is mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail, like the can; also to shift or budge slightly.

clue.text: Passage not paid to be sacred

parts.note: a hall or hallway is a passage in a house
money owed has not yet been paid

explanation.surface: A corridor with outstanding bills is somehow holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed ground is holy ground, blessed and revered.

parts.note: upper means higher or superior
a cut is a share, as of profits

explanation.surface: A larger portion for a farmhand making hay.
explanation.walkthrough: A haymaker is a wild swinging punch, not a farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising punch to the chin that could become a knockout blow.

clue.text: Stage the farm plot is worked

indicators.note: worked suggests ploughing, but here the letters of farm plot are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A phase in which the field of the farm gets cultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage from which a speaker or performer addresses people.

clue.text: Was first to leave stingers with stingers

indicators.note: to leave says a letter departs from the insects' name

parts.note: wasps are insects that sting

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Was

explanation.surface: An insect went first as stinging creatures gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: W, the first letter of 'Was', leaves WASPS; snakes are the second set of stingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous snakes, such as Cleopatra's, which bite rather than sting but are crossword 'stingers'.

explanation.surface: A methodical member of a ward's staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and methodical; also an attendant who does routine jobs on a ward.

indicators.note: in places the obstruction inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales and England
let is an old word for hinder, as in tennis or 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Taking out an obstruction from a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase or strike out, as with text.

clue.text: Where one can play with seven

definitions.text: Where one can play with seven

parts.words: Where one can play with seven
parts.note: a place to gamble, where a seven on the dice or on slot reels decides a stake

explanation.walkthrough: Seven is the key number in craps and lucky sevens on fruit machines, both found in a gambling house.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house offering dice, card and wheel games.

clue.text: Mother may enquire of the cloth

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: A mother asks a question of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' suggests the clergy; the definition is just 'cloth', a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich patterned fabric, often silk or linen, originally from Damascus.

explanation.surface: People from Belgium who are feudal subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as LIEGE MEN: men from Liège, a Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal subjects bound to serve a lord; also, read in two words, men of Liège in Belgium.

clue.text: A tarts upset at the layers

indicators.note: upset overturns the order of the letters of A tarts

explanation.surface: A bakery tray of pastries tipped over onto its layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological beds of rock lying one above another.

indicators.note: outside picks the letters at the very start and end of marine
borders picks the first and last letters of Spanish

explanation.surface: A soldier secures the Spanish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock and engage.

parts.note: read 'Increase' as 'in crease', standing in the batting crease where a left-arm wrist-spinner aims

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a delivery from a left-arm wrist-spin bowler; the stumps stand in the crease, the line marked on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The three stumps and bails a bowler aims at, standing in the crease.

parts.note: a woman's name that is also the plant called speedwell

explanation.walkthrough: 'She' points to a girl's name; 'speed well' is the speedwell, a wild flower whose botanical genus has that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the genus of small blue-flowered plants known as speedwell.

indicators.note: extremes are the ends, so take the first and last letters of deja-vu

parts.note: ties are drawn games

explanation.surface: A sense of déjà vu brings on a feeling of being bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks one is bound to perform; responsibilities.

clue.text: First see son of Noah with sweet Irish emblem

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of see

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons
rock is a hard stick of seaside candy

explanation.surface: A visitor first meets Noah's son, who brings an Irish token and a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is a British seaside sweet, a hard sugar stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the traditional symbol of Ireland.
